context:
Goal: a change merged into an already reviewed PR is still checked, and the batch runner does not repeat work that your earlier ruling said is not owed.
Problem (rule): two of your rulings disagree about one act: a plain merge of main into a reviewed PR. One says it needs no new review; the other, as drafted, says it needs a fresh fix verifier and a fresh review record. Today runner 10 pushed a plain merge of main into #3318 (your rush) and read the stricter one. The records cannot both stand, so it needs your word.
Based on (ruling): your words of 14:07 CST Nov 10, ruling R1: "i agree on letting it survive a clean merge where batch ci sees the problem rather than asecond review; i agree it shd be mechanical tooo". Decision pr-review-record holds it (line 78, "Owner's ruling": no fix check and no fresh review are owed; lines 16, 82 and 130 say the same).
Based on (ruling): your "a" of 13:12 CST Nov 13 to the coordinator's standing-grant question, and your item 806 d of 23:40 CST Nov 13 (ruling runner-merge-main-grant). The stricter line (decision standing-merge-grant, line 18: "Each new head gets a fix verifier and a fresh review log.") is in the grant text drafted from your "a", not in your quoted words, and item 806 as shown to you does not carry it. Whether you saw it is unknown.
Based on (read): relayed by the coordinator at 18:16 CST, not read by triage: the two records as above, and runner 10 reading the grant line on #3318 today. What protects the outcome now: CI on the merge head, plus the merge tool's proof that the merge is clean. Cost of the stricter line as read: one fix verifier, one record and one lane lint per updated PR, one after another. Measured today (the coordinator at 18:18 CST, from runner 10's read, log reviewed20.log; triage read none): runner 10 ran merge --reviewed at #3318's merged head 560779de5af0: "no lint: no lane-lint PASS names this head". The tool asked for NO fix verifier and NO new record. So the tool applies pr-review-record (a clean merge of main keeps the log), not line 18. Sample: 1 PR here (#3318), plus the earlier #3212 merge today (tool accepted, no round 3); the same read at #3250, #3251, #3396 and #3431 (done at their heads) and #3425 (done, CI pending). Measured cost of the stricter line: none yet.
Departs from: main — standing-merge-grant asks a fix verifier and a fresh review log for each new head, and pr-review-record asks none for a clean merge of main — one of them changes.
Meanwhile: #3318: the coordinator stopped the lane's fix verifier, because the tool read the head as done without one (see the measure above). The coordinator recommends none of the options. No option is starred.
home: decisions standing-merge-grant (line 18) and pr-review-record (lines 16, 78, 82, 130); rulings R1, runner-merge-main-grant; PR #3318

options.gain: The two records agree, and runner 10 stops one verifier, one record and one lint for each PR it updates.
options.label: Reword the grant line: a clean merge of main takes no fix verifier, and pr-review-record governs
options.lose: A merge of main into a reviewed PR is checked only by CI and the tree proof. Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo.

options.gain: The two records agree, and each merge of main into a reviewed PR gets a fresh check.
options.label: Reword pr-review-record (lines 16, 78, 82, 130): a clean merge of main needs a fresh fix verifier and record
options.lose: It undoes your 14:07 Nov 10 ruling R1, and each PR update costs one verifier, one record and one lint, one after another (measured cost: none yet).

options.label: Leave both records as they are; runner 10 reads the grant line for each PR
options.lose: The two records keep disagreeing, and every PR update asks the same question again.

title: Two of your rulings disagree on a plain merge of main into a reviewed PR: R1 says no new review, the grant line says a fresh fix verifier and record. Reword the grant line (a), reword the record (b), or leave both (c)?
why: Runner 10 read the stricter grant line on #3318 today, though your ruling R1 says a clean merge needs no new review. Only you can say which stands.
